Relats BSC · Balance Score Card

Mock-up · proposal
Dashboard review · October 2026

What the top is missing and why

The dashboard carries around forty cards, all drawn with the same chart and grouped by department. This is what we propose changing: a header strip that answers “how are we doing?” in three seconds, the indicators regrouped into the four perspectives of a scorecard, and a way of drawing each KPI that shows the variance instead of hiding it. Every figure on this page is yours, read from the dashboard of 7 October.

September 2026 · 9 of 12 months 13 on target 2 at risk 2 off target 0 no data 17 KPIs in this mock-up

1 · The header strip

The four you already have, plus the customer KPI (OTD) and the cost one (Headcount), which are what the four perspectives still need. Each card gives the value, where it should be by now, how far it moved since last month and the shape of the year. Colour always comes with a symbol, so status never rides on red and green alone. Under the title you'll find the Metabase visualization and its grid size, so it can be built straight away.

Look at the first two. Sales Turnover and Revenue sit side by side and say different things: 95M€ of 200M€, and 120M€ of 150M€. Today that stays hidden because neither shows the proportion; placed like this, it jumps out.

2 · The strip you already built, and what it's missing

Four cards went in at the top on 1 October. That is the right move. What they are missing is what makes a header strip earn its place: where we should be at this point in the year, how far it moved since last month and the shape of the year. A red dot says we are behind, but not by how much, nor since when.

At the top of this page is the same information built with Progress and Trend, which Metabase already ships. Same data, same queries, nothing custom.

2b · One detail card, before and after

Same KPI, same data. On the left, as it looks today. On the right, with the variance painted onto the bar, the commitment drawn over it, the months not yet closed in grey, and three labels instead of twenty-four. The chart on the right is a Metabase Combo (Bar + Line), 8 × 5 on the grid.

3 · The scorecard in four perspectives

This is the substantive change. The same seventeen KPIs, none added, grouped the way a Balanced Scorecard works rather than by department: people make the processes run, the processes show up at the customer, and the customer lands in the P&L. It reads bottom up — and that is how the dashboard stops saying only what is happening and starts saying why.

4 · What the review found

Worst first. The three marked Critical are data problems and worth closing before touching any design: a scorecard that contradicts itself loses the room.

  1. New
    The header strip is in, and it shows

    Since 1 October there are four cards at the top. That is the right move. What they are missing is what makes a header strip work: where we should be by now, how far it moved and the shape of the year. Right now they are three lines of text and a coloured dot, and the dot does not say by how much.

  2. New
    Two different revenues, side by side

    Revenue reads 120M€ against a 150M€ yearly target and Sales Turnover 95M€ against 200M€, in the same strip. If they are different things the titles must say so; if they are not, one of them is redundant. It is the first thing anyone reads.

  3. New
    DMI is already fixed

    The digital maturity card now shows Baseline 2.52 · Mid-Year 2.57 · Current 2.6 · Yearly 2.62. That is exactly the shape the other cards should have: the reference, where we are and where we are going.

  4. Critical
    “Yearly Actual” is not yearly

    For EBIT, SG&A, Hit Rate, Headcount, Cash Conversion, OTD and Inventory the column shows the value of September, not any yearly figure. On Sales Turnover it matches the year-to-date and on Lead Generation it looks like a sum. Three rules under one name — and each is compared against the yearly target, which is why the flow KPIs come out red by construction.

  5. Critical
    Two identical cards with opposite colours

    % Customer NCs/Delivered batches and % Total CoPQ/total sales carry the same series (1.5 · 1.48 · 1.45 · 1.42 · 1.4 · 1.37 · 1.4 · 1.4 · 1.45), the same target (1.7→1.5) and the same yearly figure (1.45 vs 1.5). One comes out all green and the other all red: one of the two has its direction inverted.

  6. Critical
    Headcount duplicated and contradictory

    Headcount Total and Average Headcount FTE share a series (1,332…1,380) and a yearly figure (1,380 / 1,456.6) but carry different targets, and the same month comes out green on one and red on the other.

  7. Data
    KPIs running on placeholder data

    R&D staff retention, TOTAL CAPEX R&D and TOTAL OPEX R&D share the same series (73.6 · 76 · 78.4 · 80 · 82.4 · 84…). So do All Project development phases and Proyecto ISO 17025. They are not wired to a source yet.

  8. Data
    Figures that cannot hold

    Real Revenue by Campaigns reads 120M€ per quarter while year-to-date Sales Turnover is 95M€: campaign revenue cannot exceed total revenue. EBIT: nine months sum to 121.9M€ against a 20M€ yearly target.

  9. Data
    The strip and the chart disagree

    The EBIT header card says the September target is 19.5M€; on the chart below it, September reads 19.1M€ and 19.5M€ falls on October. Worth checking where each one comes from: if the strip and the detail disagree, both lose credibility.

  10. Data
    Units and directions

    Average Delivery Delay / OTD measures a delay in euros. % Staff vs MOD/MOI treats the monthly figure as “lower is better” and the yearly one as “higher is better”. Lead Generation leaves most months with no status.

  11. Design
    Forty identical charts

    Every card is the same combination of grey bars, dotted blue line and coloured dot. Nothing stands out, so nothing catches the eye when it should. A scorecard has to answer “how are we doing?” in three seconds.

  12. Design
    The yearly bar shares an axis with the months

    On Sales Turnover the monthly bars reach 95M€ and the yearly target bar 200M€: the yearly one flattens the series and the trend disappears, which is exactly what you want to look at.

  13. Design
    The bars carry no information

    On Headcount, 1,332 to 1,380 is a 3.6% spread: every bar looks the same. All the information sits in the label and the chart is decoration.

  14. Design
    A thousand numbers, and colour only

    Around 24 labels per chart, many rotated 90°, across some 40 cards. And status rides entirely on red and green, which around 8% of men cannot reliably tell apart.

5 · Where we would start

STEP 1

Fix the contradictions

Decide what “Yearly Actual” means, apply it to every card, and correct the inverted directions and the duplicates.

Half a day · no chart touched

STEP 2

Regroup into four perspectives

Move the cards that already exist into four sections. No new data and no new chart: it is reordering. The per-department views stay as back tabs.

Two hours · dragging only

STEP 3

Build the header strip

The six cards at the top with the Trend and Progress visualizations Metabase already ships. Nothing custom.

Half a day · stock Metabase

STEP 4

Redraw the cards

Take the yearly bar off the monthly axis, paint the variance onto the bar and hide the months not yet closed. Can be done block by block.

In phases · one department at a time
